overview: This map shows all 230 companies in YC Summer 2026. 164 fall into eight groups. The other 66 don't share a clear group and are shown in grey. The tour takes three minutes; interrupt it anytime.

groups.name: AI-native service firms
groups.rubric: The company describes itself as the service provider (firm, practice, agency, brokerage, insurer, BPO, clinic) rather than software sold to one.
groups.narration: 24 companies describe themselves as the service firm itself, not software sold to one. Billow, Rational and Last Accounting Company are accounting firms. Florin and Princeps are insurance companies. Peer is a freight brokerage.

groups.name: Agent infrastructure
groups.rubric: Infrastructure whose users are AI agents or the developers running them: gateways, routing, inference, identity, payments, hosting, developer environments.
groups.narration: 27 companies build infrastructure for AI agents: payments, identity, hosting and routing. Agentcard lets agents buy things online. Inkbox provides identity and communication. machine0 describes itself as AWS for agents.

groups.name: Data and evals for AI labs
groups.rubric: Sells training data, evaluations, benchmarks, RL environments or simulations used to train or test AI models.
groups.narration: 24 companies sell data, evaluations or training environments to AI labs. Markov sells expert computer-use data. Petrarch sells internal industrial data. Tokenless finds flaws in RL environments and evals.

groups.name: Defense
groups.rubric: Builds for military, defense, government security or contested environments.
groups.narration: 13 companies build for defense: drone swarms from Earendil and Greypoint, radar from Vernius, exoskeletons from Edgerun, rocket cargo from Hop Aero. Isengard lists 30 people, the largest team in the batch.

groups.name: Robotics
groups.rubric: Builds robots, drones or autonomous physical systems, or the core infrastructure to run them.
groups.narration: 22 companies build robots for specific jobs. Grip handles waste, Salem works in hazardous spaces, and Proprio maintains data centers. Nori lists a humanoid robot at 1,688 dollars.

groups.name: Compute and chips
groups.rubric: Works on compute supply: chips, semiconductors, data centers, compute markets or energy for compute.
groups.narration: 16 companies work on compute: chips, data centers and markets. Computable is building a derivatives exchange for compute. Touchmark is a market for future inference capacity. Atomarine is building floating, nuclear-powered data centers.

groups.name: Vertical operations
groups.rubric: Sells AI that runs the day-to-day operations of one kind of business (an operating system, back office, or AI workforce for a named industry).
groups.narration: 26 companies sell AI that runs the operations of one kind of business: auto shops, hotels, restaurants, wholesale distributors. Bernard, with nine people, builds AI employees for home-appliance repair companies.

groups.name: Bio, chemistry and materials
groups.rubric: Works in biology, medicine development, chemistry, materials or consumer health science.
groups.narration: 12 companies work in biology, chemistry or materials. TareBio is developing vaccines for cancer and infection. Gamgee is working on cancer, starting with dogs. Molagri makes resistance-free pesticides.
